definition: LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation) is a parameter-efficient fine-tuning technique for large language models and other deep neural networks.
details: Introduced in 2021 by researchers at Microsoft, LoRA enables adaptation of pre-trained models to specific tasks while requiring significantly fewer computational resources and trainable parameters than traditional full model fine-tuning.

explainer.lead: A parameter-efficient fine-tuning technique for large language models and other deep networks, introduced in 2021 by Microsoft researchers. It matters because it adapts models at far lower compute and parameter cost than full fine-tuning.

tiers.eli5: Rather than repainting the whole house, you stick on a few removable decals that change how it looks for a specific occasion.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers freeze base weights and train small low-rank updates, drastically cutting memory and storage; a pitfall is expecting one adapter to match full fine-tuning on every task.
tiers.paperLevel: Freezes the original weights and adds a small trainable low-rank decomposition to each, reducing trainable parameters by orders of magnitude.

explainer.example: A team fine-tunes a large base model for customer-support tone by training a tiny adapter, storing megabytes instead of a full model copy.
